abstracts.value: We investigate the control and protection of two-qubit entanglement through engineered interactions between two auxiliary harmonic oscillators. Each qubit is coupled to a local oscillator via a dephasing interaction, while the oscillators interact through independently tunable position-position and momentum-momentum couplings. Employing the characteristic-function representation, we obtain analytical solutions for the composite-system dynamics and examine how the stability properties of the coupled oscillators determine the evolution of two-qubit concurrence. Our analysis reveals distinct dynamical regimes exhibiting entanglement revivals, suppression, or decay, and identifies configurations in which oscillator interactions effectively reduce entanglement degradation. We further investigate the influence of thermal dissipation using local and global master-equation descriptions, demonstrating that suitable oscillator couplings can preserve substantial two-qubit entanglement under the dissipative conditions considered. These results establish a connection between the dynamical stability of auxiliary bosonic modes and the controllability of entanglement in discrete-variable quantum systems, providing a potential strategy for entanglement protection through engineered oscillator interactions.

titles.title: Modulation and protection of entanglement in a two-qubit system via two interacting oscillator control

abstracts.value: Detection of the redshifted 21-cm signal from neutral hydrogen requires precise control of systematic effects arising from instrumental calibration. In this work, we investigate the impact of both time- and frequency-dependent residual gain and bandpass errors on the estimation of the multifrequency angular power spectrum (MAPS) using radio interferometric observations. We discuss our previously developed analytical framework for estimating bias and excess variance in 21-cm signal MAPS in the presence of these residual errors and apply it to uGMRT Band-3 observations. The statistical properties of the residual gains are derived from the data themselves, including their temporal and spectral correlations. We introduce a robust technique for additionally flagging poor-quality data. Our results show that the excess variance induced by residual gain and bandpass errors dominates over the bias across the range of angular multipoles considered. The amplitude of this variance is comparable to the expected power spectrum upper limit at redshift $z \sim 2.2$, indicating that residual calibration errors can significantly affect the detectability of the 21-cm signal. We further transform the estimated MAPS into ($k_{\perp}, k_{ll}$) space and find the expected foreground wedge structure. Importantly, we observe a significant power leakage into the nominal EoR window, which we attribute to residual calibration systematics. This highlights that even after standard foreground mitigation, time- and frequency-correlated gain errors can introduce mode-mixing and contaminate the EoR window. Our results emphasise the necessity of improved calibration accuracy and robust characterisation of residual gain statistics for current and upcoming interferometric experiments such as the uGMRT and SKA, to enable reliable detection of the cosmological 21-cm signal.

titles.title: Calibration requirements for Epoch of Reionization 21-cm signal observations - V. Bias and variance in the cylindrical power spectrum from uGMRT Band 3 observations of the ELAIS-N1 field

abstracts.value: Set coherence is a quantum resource for a set of states that characterizes whether a collection of quantum states contains coherence, namely whether these states fail to be simultaneously incoherent in a common basis. In this work, we show that the free operations of set coherence are common commutativity-preserving quantum channels, from which we then establish an axiomatic framework for set-coherence measure (SCM). Within this framework, we investigate the robustness based measures deduced by taking, respectively, the average, maximum, and sum of the single-state robustnesses over a common reference basis, where the first two were previously introduced in the literature and we check here whether they satisfy our SCM axioms. Consequently, we show that the averaged robustness is an SCM but it is neither unified nor complete, the maximal robustness is a unified SCM but is neither complete nor strongly superadditive, whereas the sum robustness is a complete SCM. Furthermore, we propose several classes of SCMs based on pairwise commutators. We show that the Schatten $p$-norm based SCMs are complete and strongly superadditive. We also find that the universal fourth-order Bargmann gap measure proposed in the literature is a complete and strongly superadditive quantifier of set coherence. Finally, we discuss the operational meaning of the SCM in the context of optimal approximate quantum broadcasting, and show that the amount of set coherence can closely reflect the performance of this task.

titles.title: Measure of set coherence

abstracts.value: Cosmic voids provide a setting for examining the interplay between mass and environment in shaping galaxy and halo properties. Using the SDSS DR7 volume-limited galaxy sample and the ELUCID constrained simulation of the local large-scale structure, we investigate the radial profiles of galaxy and subhalo properties across different mass ranges, identifying voids independently in the observed galaxy and simulated subhalo distributions. Both stellar mass and subhalo mass increase from void interiors toward the void boundary, indicating that lower-mass galaxies and subhaloes preferentially reside in void interiors. The satellite fraction of subhaloes also increases systematically toward the void boundary. Galaxy colour and specific star formation rate exhibit radial variations that are weaker than their dependence on stellar mass, while the spiral fraction shows little radial dependence at fixed stellar mass. For dark-matter haloes, the apparent radial increase in size within a broad high-mass bin largely disappears when narrower mass ranges are considered. Halo concentration and spin show radial variations at fixed mass, with higher concentrations and lower spins toward void interiors, although the concentration trend is less pronounced in the extended low-mass sample. The formation redshift of low-mass subhaloes also increases toward the void boundary, whereas this dependence weakens and eventually disappears at higher masses. Overall, the radial trends in galaxy properties are generally weaker than their mass dependence, while several subhalo properties retain measurable radial variations at fixed mass.

titles.title: Radial dependence of galaxy and halo properties in cosmic voids: SDSS DR7 and the ELUCID constrained simulation

abstracts.value: We developed a new theoretical approach in the description of partonic structure of hadrons based on spectral function representation of valence quarks. In this approach massless valence quarks are considered in the mean field of residual hadron. This approach initially was applied to the calculation of parton distribution function~(PDF) of nucleons that resulted in an observation of pion-cloud structure of nucleon. In this report we present our calculation of pion PDF in the valence region within the same approach. In this approach we describe the soft partonic structure of pion through the valence $q\bar q$ cluster, embedded in the residual field of the pion. The pion PDF is calculated using phenomenological Light-Front wave functions for the $q\bar q$ cluster and the residual field. Our result indicates that the peak position of the x weighted valence PDF~(xPDF) depends on parameters characterizing the virtuality of the $q\bar q$ cluster and the mass of the residual system. These parameters are evaluated by fitting the calculated PDF to the height and the peak position of empirical pion xPDF at starting $Q_0$. They indicate that unlike the nucleon case, very little residual mass is needed in the pion to describe existing pion PDFs in the valence region. They also require the $q\bar q$-cluster to be highly virtual with the interacting quark carrying almost all of the momentum of the $q\bar q$ cluster. This picture is consistent with the dominance of the Feynman mechanism leaving little room for the hard component in the PDF. The calculation practically describes the $\sim (1-x)$ behavior observed recently at $x\to 1$ limit. Our non-trivial observation is that the height and the peak position of xPDF define the analytic behavior of valence PDF at $x\to 1$ limit.

titles.title: The Pion Parton Distribution Puzzle in the High x Region

abstracts.value: The $b_1(1235)$ state has a sizable decay width, which have longstanding puzzle in treating as a final state in theoretical calculations may lead to systematic deviations in the predicted observables. To address this issue and further explore the internal structure of this resonance, we study the multi-body semileptonic decays $B_{\ell4}$ and $B_{\ell6}$. Within the approximation where the $b_1(1235)$ resonance dominates, we study the $B_{\ell4}$ decay $B\to b_1(1235)(\toωπ)\ell^+ν_\ell$ in the QCD light-cone sum rules framework. The corresponding transition form factors (TFFs) are calculated by constructing a correlation function with a right-handed chiral current. As the main nonperturbative input for the TFFs calculation, the transverse twist-2 light-cone distribution amplitude (LCDA) of the $b_1(1235)$ resonance is constructed using the light-cone harmonic oscillator model, and the resulting LCDA exhibits a single-peak behavior. At the large-recoil region, we obtain the TFFs $V_{0, 1, 2}(0)$ and $A(0)$, together with the corresponding TFFs ratios $r_V = 1.530_{-0.016}^{+0.013}$ and $r_2 = 0.553_{-0.015}^{+0.012}$. We then further study the complete $B_{\ell4}$ decay by incorporating the $b_1(1235)\toωπ$ resonant line shape and obtain the corresponding observables. The results show that the branching ratio of the $B_{\ell4}$ decay is about $1/3$ of that obtained when $b_1(1235)$ is treated as a final state. We also account for the subsequent decay $ω\to π^+π^-π^0$ and further predicted the branching ratio of the $B_{\ell6}$ decay $B\to b_1(1235)(\toω(\to π^+π^-π^0)π)\ell^+ν_\ell$. These results may provide useful references for future experimental measurements and further theoretical studies.

titles.title: Analysis of $S$-wave $ωπ$ dynamics behavior in multi-body $B_{\ell4}$ and $B_{\ell6}$ decays

abstracts.value: Driving the plasma wakefield with a train of multiple particle bunches has the potential to significantly increase the accelerated charge, provided that the witness bunches also form a train. In this scenario, the driver bunches can replenish the wave energy after the passage of the witness bunches, yielding comparable charges in both trains. However, implementing this method at high wakefield amplitudes is complicated by the reshaping of the driver bunches as they reach radial equilibrium with the wave. The witness bunches cannot preserve their quality during this process; nevertheless, they must load the wave to prevent it from reaching the amplitude at which the wakefield period elongates and the wave destroys the driver. The proposed solution is to form an equilibrium train of initially inefficient driver bunches, which becomes efficient upon the injection of the witness bunches. This concept is demonstrated using the example of a self-modulating driver beam. Several factors favoring a high witness charge are identified: injecting additional ``phaser'' bunches at the zero-accelerating-field points, suppressing the formation of an electron halo around the plasma, and operating at the highest possible wakefield amplitudes.

titles.title: Maximization of accelerated charge in multibunch-driven plasma wakefield accelerators

abstracts.value: Models for X-ray spectroscopy involving complex relativistic or plasma physics are commonly pre-computed on a grid, In this paper, we aim to quantify the potential biases and distortions introduced by the computational error and propagated into parameter inference by interpolating linearly these complex, non-linear models. We analyse the performance of Bayesian sampling algorithms on mock inference problems. Then, we model real observations of an accreting black hole X-ray binary in both the soft and hard states. We find that linear interpolation can a) greatly bias the posterior distribution of model parameters and b) distort the likelihood space to such a degree that posterior distributions become artificially multimodal. This multi-modality causes a noticeable loss in computational efficiency in both sampling and fitting techniques. As a result, exploring a given parameter space until convergence requires an extremely large computational cost. These findings call for improving the computational techniques used when fitting modern X-ray data, for example through better sampling algorithms and/or more sophisticated interpolation schemes

titles.title: The biases caused by interpolated table models and their impact on X-ray spectroscopy

abstracts.value: The suppression of strange hadrons in pp and p--Pb collisions at the LHC, including the $ϕ$ meson, has recently been described by the exact conservation of strangeness imposed on the quarks of a causally connected cluster before hadronization. Here we extend this approach to the light flavors. The numbers of up and down quarks and antiquarks are conserved in the same cluster, and the suppression of a baryon or a nucleus depends only on how many light quarks of each flavor it contains. With the strangeness sector fixed by the previous analysis, a single constant, the ratio $r$ of light to strange quark abundances, determines the multiplicity dependence of protons, deuterons, He and hypertriton in pp and p--Pb collisions. Including the finite size of the nuclei, one obtains a very good fit of the data for $r=3.76\pm0.38$, i.e. strange quarks about 0.27 times as abundant as light quarks per flavor, close to the value known from string fragmentation

titles.title: Exact flavor conservation at the quark level in causal clusters: strange particles, protons and light nuclei in small collision systems

abstracts.value: Extragalactic fast X-ray transients (EFXTs) detected by the Einstein Probe are extending the parameter space of relativistic stellar explosions toward softer and longer-lived transients. Here we report EP251129a/GRB 251129A at z=0.505, which exhibits two X-ray plateaus: an early plateau lasting $\sim 10^{4}\,\rm s$ followed by a rapid decay with spectral softening, and a second plateau extending to 60 days, placing it at the extreme long-duration end of Gamma Ray Burst (GRB) plateaus. The early optical emission evolves independently of the X-ray, indicating a different origin; whereas the unusual radio afterglow shows a rapid rise of $F_ν\propto t^{1.9-2.5}$ and a delayed peak at $\sim36-40$ days, providing strong evidence for an off-axis geometry. We find that the early X-ray behavior resembles those of ultra-long GRBs (ULGRBs) and can be naturally explained by the internal dissipation from a newborn millisecond magnetar undergoing gravitational-wave-dominated spin-down before collapsing into a black hole. The early optical, radio and late X-ray emission are well described by an off-axis two-component jet afterglow with additional energy injection, possibly powered by fallback accretion onto black hole. EP251129a therefore connects the emerging EFXT population with ULGRB-like central-engine activity and off-axis afterglow, offering a rare opportunity to probe both the evolution of central engine and jet structure in a single event.

titles.title: EP251129a: A Fast X-ray Transient with Two X-Ray Plateaus and Its Off-axis Afterglow

abstracts.value: We study light top-flavoured dark matter (DM) below the electroweak (EW) scale within the dark Standard Model effective field theory (DSMEFT). We perform the one-loop matching of the DSMEFT onto the dark low-energy effective field theory (DLEFT) at the EW scale for all relevant operators that couple scalar, fermionic or vector DM, as well as axion-like particles, exclusively to third-generation quarks. After QCD evolution to the relevant low-energy scales, we match the DLEFT onto the non-relativistic EFT for DM-nucleus scattering. This EFT chain provides a unified framework for phenomenological studies of rare $B$- and $K$-meson decays with missing energy, direct and indirect detection, and the thermal relic abundance. Interpreting the Belle II excess in $B^+\to K^+ν\barν$ as a decay into DM, we find that only the DSMEFT operators contributing at tree level can accommodate it with $O(1)$ couplings for a new-physics scale of $1\,\mathrm{TeV}$. The decay $B^0\to K^{*0}+\mathrm{inv}$ provides the strongest constraint over large portions of the Belle II-favoured parameter space, while $K^+\toπ^++\mathrm{inv}$ can dominate at low and $B_s\to\mathrm{inv}$, $B^+\toπ^++\mathrm{inv}$ and $Υ(1S)\to\mathrm{inv}$ become important at high DM masses, respectively. Direct-detection searches by CRESST-III and DarkSide-50 are competitive for operators involving scalar quark currents and, depending on the operator, exclude the Belle~II-favoured band for $m_{\mathrm{DM}}\gtrsim1$-$2\,\mathrm{GeV}$. We also perform detailed analyses of the thermal relic abundance and the indirect-detection constraints from the CMB and Fermi-LAT.

titles.title: Light top-flavoured dark matter in dark SMEFT: one-loop matching and phenomenology

abstracts.value: We derive the mass formulas and more accurate asymptotic expressions for the densities of states for string models of hadrons with one fixed heavy endpoint or a baryon junction. We show that strings with one fixed endpoint have the same Hagedorn temperature as ordinary open strings at the same tension and number of polarizations, despite the different Regge slopes of heavy-light and light mesons. This provides a microscopic explanation for the universality of the Hagedorn temperature recently found phenomenologically. We also find that the baryon-junction and quark-diquark pictures share this Hagedorn temperature and yield the same asymptotic mass dependence of the density of states, differing only by an overall normalization. The observed baryon mass spectrum provides little discrimination between the two pictures, although the baryon-junction model has a larger discrepancy with the observed Regge slopes.

abstracts.value: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) show diverse temporal morphologies, shaped both by their intrinsic emission and by propagation effects such as residual dispersion and multipath scattering. Because several of these effects can broaden a burst asymmetrically, an asymmetric profile does not by itself establish multipath scattering. We measure the frequency dependence of the temporal tail in FRB 20210415C, a bright burst from the repeating source FRB 20210219C. The burst is detected across approximately 400-800 MHz. Frequency-resolved fits yield an empirical exponential-tail timescale, $τ_{\rm emp}$, that follows $τ_{\rm emp}\proptoν^α$. Two complementary treatments of the underlying pulse width give $α=-3.95\pm0.07$ and $-4.14\pm0.08$. Both results are consistent with the commonly adopted $ν^{-4}$ scattering law. The inferred scattering time is approximately 8.0 ms at 583 MHz, exceeding Galactic foreground estimates by a factor of at least $4\times10^{2}$. This favours a dominant contribution beyond the Milky Way, although the data do not localise the scattering screen. FRB 20210415C therefore provides a direct measurement of a scattering law commonly imposed in catalogue analyses.

titles.title: A frequency-resolved measurement of the scattering law in FRB 20210415C

abstracts.value: In canonical twisted-torus models of hydromagnetic equilibrium in neutron stars, the toroidal field is confined to regions where the poloidal field lines are closed. As spindown torques applied at the stellar surface need not be communicated efficiently to such magnetically-unlocked regions, toroidal zones or magnetic voids may rotate faster than the electromagnetically braked part of the star. Continuous gravitational radiation from the associated non-corotating quadrupole may therefore be emitted at higher frequencies than poloidal ones to a degree that depends on the diffusive microphysics controlling angular momentum transport. Dissipative processes can suppress long-lived lags, and we estimate the relevant timescales and their sensitivity to microphysics. Nevertheless, we show that a quadrupole component whose pattern speed differs from the observed spin is shifted, or smeared, over a finite frequency band. Single-template or narrowband upper limits therefore constrain only the quadrupole contribution lying inside the searched frequency window, not necessarily the full frequency-integrated quadrupole. Using simple models, we quantify this spectral redistribution over finite observation windows and discuss its implications for continuous-wave searches.

titles.title: Torque lags from magnetic unlocking in neutron stars and gravitational-wave smearing

abstracts.value: We propose an arbitrary waveform generation architecture based on charge-coupled devices (CCDs) for qubit control. Waveform samples are stored as charge packets in CCD channels and sequentially clocked out as voltage samples. Multiple channels are operated in parallel and time-interleaved to achieve high effective sampling rates. The generated baseband waveforms are then upconverted to microwave frequencies to drive qubit operations. By representing waveform information as stored charge rather than as continuously generated or transmitted microwave signals, the proposed architecture provides a path to reducing cryogenic interconnect density and lowering heat load in scalable quantum control systems.

abstracts.value: We present the first computation of the $π^+π^+$ scattering length in large-$N$ QCD in the 't Hooft limit, $N_{\scriptscriptstyle{\rm f}}/N\to 0$, using the twisted Eguchi--Kawai formulation of the lattice theory. abstracts.value: We characterize the exact trade-off between internal and external entanglement in asymmetric two-mode Gaussian states at fixed local symplectic eigenvalues. Internal entanglement is quantified by the negativity $\mathcal{N}_{A:B}$ between the two modes, while external entanglement is quantified by the negativity $\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD}$ across a Gaussian purification. Numerical sampling suggests the boundary structure of the attainable region in the $(\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD},\mathcal{N}_{A:B})$ plane, which we then determine analytically. Parametrizing the global symplectic spectrum yields a closed admissible interval for the remaining spectral parameter at fixed $\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD}$. We prove constructively that every point in this interval corresponds to a physical covariance matrix, implying that all intermediate values of $\mathcal{N}_{A:B}$ between the resulting sharp bounds are achievable. The upper bound is attained for opposite-sign correlations of equal magnitude, while the positive branch of the lower bound occurs when one global symplectic eigenvalue equals unity. We also identify two external-entanglement thresholds, derive a saturated monogamy-type inequality, and recover the symmetric-state limit.

titles.title: Complete characterization of internal-external entanglement trade-offs in two-mode Gaussian states

abstracts.value: The hybrid reconstruction algorithm developed by Cibrario et al. 2023 combined a convolutional neural network (CNN) with standard moment analysis to improve track reconstruction in IXPE Gas Pixel Detectors. Although validated on laboratory data (Cibrario et al. 2025), the method's astrophysical performance had not been systematically characterized. We present the first comparison of hybrid and standard reconstruction on IXPE point sources, measuring sensitivity gains versus energy. We analyze Her X-1, a bright, polarized accreting pulsar as a benchmark, and soft-state XTE J1701-461, a bright neutron-star low-mass X-ray binary with no detected polarization, to assess residual systematics. From both pipelines' Level-2 event files, we compare normalized Stokes parameters, polarization degree (PD) and angle (PA), and detection significance. For Her X-1, hybrid reconstruction increases significance at all energies, significantly above ~2.83 keV. R = σ_hyb/σ_std differs from unity by 9.3σ in the 2.83-4.00 keV bin and reaches 1.18±0.03 at 5.66-8.00 keV (6.2σ). For XTE J1701-461, PD is consistent with zero and R with unity. Fourier analysis reveals excess power in hybrid angle distributions at low energies for modes m = 3, 6, 12 and 15, significant at >7σ relative to the standard method; at 5-8 keV, all modes are consistent with noise in both methods. These CNN-amplified hexagonal-grid artifacts do not affect Stokes parameters because they are orthogonal to polarization modes.The method delivers a statistically significant sensitivity gain for Her X-1, consistent with Cibrario et al. 2025 and equivalent to ~20% more effective area without extra observing time. These results support systematic use of hybrid reconstruction on IXPE astrophysical data.

titles.title: Comparison of Hybrid and Standard Reconstruction Methods on IXPE Astrophysical Data

abstracts.value: Causal self-dual nonlinear electrodynamics admits a simple auxiliary-field description: the Lagrangian is linear in the two Lorentz invariants of the field strength, and the dynamics is encoded in a potential $W(φ)$ of a single auxiliary variable. We study non-perturbative $T\bar T$-like flows of these theories in this formalism. The irrelevant (stress-tensor) deformation acts on the potential by a rescaling, while the marginal ModMax-type deformation translates its vacuum. We derive the resulting flow equations exactly, show that the irrelevant exact $T\bar T$-like flow takes the autonomous form $\partial_λ\mathcal L=X\,F(r)$, where the closed form kernel $F$ depends only on the ratio $r=-T^μ_μ/\sqrt{4X-Y}$ of stress-tensor invariants. We also give an explicit reconstruction of the auxiliary potential from a given kernel. Causality imposes the differential inequality $D(r)>1/(1-r)$, while a globally single-valued kernel requires the ratio $r$ to be monotonic along the auxiliary branch. We examine the relation between the evenness of the exact $T\bar T$-like flow , the $φ$-parity of the potential, and the analyticity of the Lagrangian in the electromagnetic invariants, including the effect of a marginal ModMax parameter. We construct the linear auxiliary and Hamiltonian formulations and show that the Hamiltonian flow is governed by the same exact $T\bar T$-like flow with the opposite sign. We also express Born's Legendre self-duality, the two characteristic cones, and the energy conditions in terms of the kernel. In particular, $r=(\varepsilon-p_\perp)/(\varepsilon+p_\perp)$ has a direct physical interpretation. Exact $T\bar T$-like flow s are obtained for generalized Born-Infeld, logarithmic, q-deformed, and no-$τ$-maximum electrodynamics.

titles.title: Exact Stress Tensor Flows in Causal Electrodynamics: Auxiliary Field Formalism

abstracts.value: A Hybrid Quantum Neural Network (HQNN) is applied to recover the photometric redshift of a galaxy dataset built using data from two astronomical surveys, the Kilo-Degree Survey (KIDS) and the VISTA Kilo-Degree Infrared Galaxy (VIKING), which provide data with coverage from the optical to the near-infrared electromagnetic spectrum. The results are then compared with those obtained by a classical neural network. We see that HQNN consistently recovers the reference photometric redshift with a high statistical fidelity. Furthermore, both the $R^2$ and the MSE found by the HQNN are consistently better than those found by the classical counterpart (albeit consistent in the error range), proving the worth of further investigating these novel technologies for this particular astrophysical application.

titles.title: Photometric Redshift Estimation with Hybrid Quantum Neural Network

abstracts.value: We investigate critical correlations in the weakly anisotropic two-dimensional scalar lattice $ϕ^4$ theory and demonstrate that a previously reported independence of the correlation length amplitude ratio from the local interaction strength does not hold. Monte Carlo simulations instead reveal a pronounced dependence of this ratio on the interaction strength. As the coupling is increased, the amplitude ratio interpolates between the continuum and Ising limits, highlighting a nontrivial interplay between lattice effects and local interactions. These findings call for a revised theoretical description of anisotropy effects at finite coupling in this prototypical lattice field theory.

titles.title: Interaction dependence of the critical correlation length amplitude ratio in anisotropic scalar lattice $ϕ^4$ theory

abstracts.value: We explore effective field theory (EFT) realizations of the dark dimension (DD) scenario in which the size of the DD is determined by the competition between a 5D quintessence potential and the Casimir energy. When only contributions from massless fields are considered, the Casimir energy does not have a typical energy scale, and the 4D dark energy (DE) scale is set by the height of the 5D quintessence potential. The simple 5D model we first study has an attractive feature that the size of the DD is related to the 4D vacuum energy (VE), as outlined above. However, it turns out that the 4D VE thus obtained cannot work as the 4D DE in the standard cosmological setting. One of the discrepancies between the VE and the DE manifests in the radion dependence of the effective 4D Newton's gravitational constant. This leads us to explore a 5D model in which the 4D Einstein-Hilbert (EH) action is dominantly induced by quantum effects, leaving the radion dependence of the 4D Newton's constant subdominant. This model leads to an attractive cosmological model, realizing the mechanism explained in the beginning. We also explore a 6D model with the total internal volume fixed, to make the 4D Newton's constant independent of the radion. We first study a scenario in which the sizes of the 5th and the 6th dimensions are of the same order. In this scenario, the physical origin of the size of the DD is left to its UV completion. Next, we turn to a scenario in which there is a large hierarchy between the sizes of the 5th and the 6th dimensions. In this scenario, the energy scale of the 5D quintessence potential turns out to be much higher than the energy scale of the 4D DE as inferred from the cosmological observations, so we need to subtract a constant term in 4D to tune the 4D DE. This prevents us from obtaining the scaling relation for the DE expected in the dSDC.

titles.title: Relating Dark Dimension Size with Dark Energy via 5D Quintessence Potential and Casimir Energy

abstracts.value: A study of resonant structures in $B^0 \to D^{*-}D^0K^+$ decays is presented. The analysis uses proton-proton collision data collected by the LHCb experiment at center-of-mass energies of $\sqrt{s} = 7$, 8, and 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 9 fb$^{-1}$. The analysis demonstrates that the existing known excited $D_s^+$ resonances in the $D^0K^+$ spectrum are insufficient to describe the data. The inclusion of the tetraquark state $T_{c\bar{c}1}(4430)^-$ improves the description of the data with a statistical significance exceeding $5σ$. This corresponds to the first observation of the $T_{c\bar{c}1}(4430)^- \to D^{*-} D^0$ decay. The measured properties of the $T_{c\bar{c}1}(4430)^-$ state are consistent with those previously measured in its decay to the $ψ(2S)π^-$ final state.

titles.title: Observation of the $T_{c\bar{c}1}(4430)^-$ state in $B^0\to D^{*-}D^0K^+$ decays

abstracts.value: We construct self-correcting 3D surface codes over $\mathbb Z_q$ with local dimension $q$ growing with system size. The model preserves the local geometry and stabilizer support of the ordinary 3D surface code and remains translation invariant in the bulk, while modifying only the stabilizer Pauli powers. We use the Lee metric to characterize error weight and consider local Metropolis dynamics with single-qudit $X^{\pm1}$ and $Z^{\pm1}$ updates, each changing the energy by at most a constant independent of $q$ and system size $N$. We prove that, below the critical temperature, when the local dimension scales as $q=Θ(N)$, the memory times in both error sectors grow at least as $\exp\left[Ω(N^{1/3})\right]$. Our numerical results further support these analytical results. Together, these results establish growing local Hilbert-space dimension as a new resource for designing self-correcting quantum memories while retaining simple local geometry and local thermal dynamics.

titles.title: Self-Correcting 3D Surface Code with Growing Local Dimension

abstracts.value: Comparing solvers for quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) requires distinguishing solution quality from optimality certification. We compare classical, tensor-network, and fixed-schedule quantum approaches on 180 benchmark instances from ten families with 14-48 variables, supplemented by harder synthetic instances with known optimal solutions, extending to 128 variables. On the main benchmark, a general-purpose branch-and-cut solver matches all reference energies and certifies 176 instances within a 600,s cap. When the known optima are moved to randomly chosen bitstrings, the search comparison changes: at n = 48 the branch-and-cut solver finds only four of ten optima and certifies none, whereas parallel tempering reaches every optimum in every tested run at a 60,s budget. Structural and trajectory diagnostics explain aspects of tensor-network performance. A treewidth bound ranks trajectory bond-dimension demand at Spearman $ρ= 0.78$ in sample and $0.73$ out of sample, but provides only a coarse runtime estimate. Controlled experiments identify excited-state trapping during warm-started density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) sweeps and demonstrate mitigation by restarting the variational search. These diagnostics do not yield a validated solver-selection rule. The tested linear-ramp quantum approximate optimization algorithm (LR-QAOA) runs offer no solution-quality improvement over the classical comparators. In the separate Wishart scaling study, on the harder setting, none of the classical methods tested reaches the optimum at the sampled sizes from n = 72 onward within the tested budgets. While this does not provide evidence for quantum advantage, it identifies a domain for further investigation.

titles.title: Comparing classical and quantum QUBO solvers: optimality, trajectory diagnostics, and limits of solver selection

abstracts.value: Dissipative algorithms for preparing thermal and ground states typically require a total Hamiltonian simulation time that grows at least linearly with system size $N$, even when their mixing time grows only polylogarithmically. We achieve sublinear simulation time for free fermions by engineering local interactions with a bath whose size grows in proportion to the system size. Starting from arbitrary initial states, our thermal state preparation algorithm achieves trace-norm error $ε$ in total simulation time $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{N}/ε)$ at fixed inverse temperature and bounded single-particle bandwidth, while ground state preparation of gapped systems requires only $\mathrm{polylog}(N/ε)$ time. We further establish lower bounds for thermal state preparation within the bath protocols considered, identifying two obstacles to faster preparation, namely fourth-order deviations from the target thermal state and fluctuations induced by a random frequency shared by all bath qubits. Our results demonstrate that the linear simulation time barrier in dissipative state preparation can be overcome and clarify the bath and filter-design constraints that govern further complexity improvements.

titles.title: Sublinear thermal state and ground state preparation for free fermions via system-bath interaction

abstracts.value: Multiplexing and photonic-electronic integration offer a route to scalable and high-throughput quantum key distribution (QKD) networks through parallel transmission and compact hardware suited to volume manufacturing. Realizing this route requires multichannel transmitters and receivers, and a security analysis accounting for mode coupling. Here we present a CMOS-compatible photonic-electronic multimode continuous-variable QKD architecture, using polarization multiplexing as a two-mode example. Silicon-photonic transmitter and receiver chips prepare and detect two polarization modes in parallel. The receiver is co-integrated with a dual-channel 28-nm CMOS transimpedance amplifier, providing shot-noise clearances exceeding 20 dB in both channels. Pilot-assisted unitary digital recovery removes the need for active optical polarization control, while a multimode security analysis accounts for the mode crosstalk. At 2 percent residual crosstalk, the multimode analysis extends the simulated secure distance from 39 to 84 km, near the crosstalk-free limit of 89 km. Over 10 km of deployed fibre, the mean total finite-size secret-key rate estimate is 6.69 Mbit/s, 12 percent above the single-mode analysis from the same digitally recovered data. These results establish a route to scalable multimode quantum-secured networks built on technology suited to mass production.

titles.title: Multimode continuous-variable quantum key distribution with CMOS-compatible photonic-electronic integration

abstracts.value: In classical simulations of quantum circuits, sampling shots (measurement outcomes) from the final state is a routine but costly step. In widely used software, including Qiskit and PennyLane, its cost grows linearly with the number of shots $S$, even when the simulation has already produced the full state vector, because every shot is generated and processed individually. If only the measurement counts are needed, this is unnecessary. The counts can be drawn directly from a multinomial distribution, decomposed into a sequence of conditional binomial draws, each performed in expected constant time by the BTPE algorithm. The sampling cost is then independent of $S$. We describe an implementation of this approach, which also shortens the computation for states whose probability is concentrated on a few outcomes, and compare it with Qiskit's sampling primitives for up to 20 qubits and $10^6$ shots. Our implementation is faster in every configuration tested, by a factor that grows with the number of shots and exceeds $10^3$ in most configurations at $S = 10^6$, and its samples are statistically indistinguishable from those of the reference implementations.

titles.title: Multinomial shot sampling for quantum circuits

abstracts.value: Hadron-based event-plane estimators can be affected by nonflow and autocorrelation biases, especially at low multiplicity. Coherent $J/ψ$ photoproduction offers a complementary geometry reference through the correlation between quasireal-photon polarization and the reaction plane. We calculate the second-order dilepton coefficient $A_2$ relative to the reaction plane in hadronic Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.36$ TeV within an equivalent-photon and generalized vector-meson-dominance Glauber framework. Nuclear diffraction and two-source interference produce a pronounced transverse-momentum dependence, while the rapidity dependence is weak. We also compare two treatments of coherent scattering in the overlap region of the two colliding nuclei. Suppressing the contribution from this region reduces the yield and strengthens the integrated polarization--reaction-plane correlation, with the largest differences in central and semicentral collisions and smaller differences toward peripheral collisions. Joint measurements of the coherent yield and $A_2$ can constrain how hadronic interactions disrupt nuclear coherence and clarify the photoproduction mechanism. With sufficient tagged yields, azimuthal correlations involving decay leptons from photoproduced $J/ψ$ mesons could complement studies of collectivity, with potential future applications to small systems.

titles.title: Dilepton azimuthal anisotropy from coherent $J/ψ$ photoproduction in hadronic Pb-Pb collisions

abstracts.value: We measure the dipole in the count of radio galaxies over the sky as seen by the Australian SKA Pathfinder (ASKAP) in the Rapid ASKAP Continuum Survey (RACS). Our analysis focuses on the third observational epoch in the 'low' passband (943.5 MHz; RACS-low3) and the first epoch in the 'mid' passband (1367.5 MHz; RACS-mid1). We find strong evidence for a systematic relation between flux density and the temperature at the time of observation, whereby reported flux densities are suppressed to a greater degree when the ASKAP antennas are warmer. We include this temperature response in our forward model as part of our Simulation-based Inference (SBI) pipeline, generating data realisations that are then used by a neural network to learn the likelihood function. Despite this model, RACS-low3 and RACS-mid1 both exhibit a dipole inconsistent with the kinematic dipole of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB), adding further evidence for the 'cosmic dipole tension'. For RACS-low3, the dipole agrees in direction but has an amplitude four times in excess, while the dipole for RACS-mid1 is offset from the CMB and has an amplitude roughly five times in excess. Our findings underscore the importance of interrogating the data for systematic effects and showcase the power of SBI in handling them.

titles.title: Cracking into RACS - I. Measuring the cosmic dipole in the RACS-low3 and RACS-mid1 radio surveys with simulation-based inference

abstracts.value: Self-exciting (Hawkes) models of epidemics, earthquakes, financial markets, and social cascades are usually calibrated with a branching ratio $n$ below one. This is a condition for stationarity, not for existence: a process with $n>1$ grows exponentially but remains finite on any finite horizon. Imposing stationarity is also misleading, because transient supercritical episodes then masquerade as near-criticality. Reconstructing the latent genealogy of events, we show that a single finite record can reveal an excursion into the regime $n(t)>1$, and back, and date its onset and end. Detectability is governed by the excess $n-1$ times the square root of the number of exposed parents. Even when the memory time of the triggering is unknown, the data determine the growth rate of activity during the episode nearly as precisely as when it is known, and hence whether $n$ crossed unity, whereas the value of $n$ requires independent knowledge of the memory time. Letting the data choose between endogenous amplification and external forcing prevents confusing the two. In the 2015 Korean MERS outbreak, our reconstruction shows that transmission by hospital cohorts had collapsed by 28 May, before the incidence peak and two weeks before the instantaneous reproduction number fell below one; in real time, it establishes the collapse a few days earlier than this standard indicator. Our framework separates stationarity, non-explosion, and transient supercritical amplification, and provides a practical route for detecting short-lived endogenous instabilities in self-exciting systems.

titles.title: Transient Supercriticality in Hawkes Processes: Detection, Identifiability, and Apparent Criticality

abstracts.value: We review how external electric fields reshape the information content of spatially confined atoms, and we contrast the response to a uniform static field with that to a monochromatic, time-dependent laser field. The central quantities are the Shannon entropies in position and momentum space, Sr and Sp, and their sum ST = Sr +Sp, which obeys the BBM bound. Using the confined hydrogen atom (CHA) and the particle in a spherical box (PISB), its tight confinement limit, as reference systems, we first show that the field-free total entropy of the CHA depends non-monotonically on the confining radius whereas that of the PISB is strictly scale invariant. We then present Stark maps of the entropies for the ten lowest m = 0 levels at the confining radius of 6 a.u. The ground-state polarizability is reduced from the free-atom value 4.5 a.u. to 4.06 a.u. in the CHA but is 46.8 a.u. in the PISB, and the entropic response of the two systems differs correspondingly.

titles.title: External-field-modified entropic exchange in confined quantum systems: static versus time-dependent electric fields

abstracts.value: In the multimode regime of cavity quantum electrodynamics (cQED), light-matter coupling can be strong enough such as to allows a quantum emitter to couple with multiple resonant field modes. This regime leaves distinctive signatures in the behavior of both the field and the emitter, which are already accessible by modern experimental techniques. To model such effects in lossy cavities, effective discrete-mode approaches have been widely employed, despite their accuracy beyond two modes remaining rarely benchmarked. In this work, we demonstrate the necessity of employing multiple modes to describe the multimode signatures by analyzing the dynamics of an atom in a one-dimensional lossy resonator. The atom's dynamics is simulated using the formalism developed in Weitzel et al. (2026) (arXiv:2512.18478), where a resonance quantization prescription is provided. We investigate its dependency with respect to two different parameters: the light-matter coupling strength and the atom's position. In the former case, we find that the minimal number of modes necessary to capture the essential features of the atom's dynamics increases with the coupling strength. In the latter, we further observe that the multimode regime leads to a strong position-dependency of the atom's dynamics. In all cases, we discuss the physical interpretation of our results and further discuss about how the employed formalism can be used to recover physically relevant quantities.

titles.title: Quantized-resonance description of a quantum emitter dynamics in a lossy multimode cavity

abstracts.value: We apply positive-unlabelled (PU) machine learning to the 1623 blazars of uncertain type (BCUs) in the Fermi Large Area Telescope Fourth Source Catalogue, Data Release 4 (4FGL-DR4). Five PU classifiers are trained on seven gamma-ray features, once with the 820 flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs) and once with the 1490 BL Lac objects as the labelled class (FSRQ mode and BL Lac mode). Each source is scored out of fold over 100 repeated five-fold splits, and its confidence is the fraction of splits in which at least three of the five classifiers flag it. At a confidence of at least 0.1, 437 BCUs are FSRQ-like, 597 are BL Lac-like, 12 are flagged in both modes and 577 in neither. On known sources the ensemble reaches a recall of 0.80 in FSRQ mode and 0.82 in BL Lac mode at a false-positive rate of 0.08, but a logistic regression trained on the labelled sources alone does at least as well, so PU learning gives no accuracy gain here. Removing the sky coordinates from the features does not lower the performance on known sources but adds 107 BCUs to the candidate lists and drops 30, which is consistent with the coordinates acting as a selection shortcut, so we exclude them. We check the candidates against published optical spectra, SDSS-V spectra, and BCUs that later received a class in the catalogue. Among sources assigned a single class, BL Lac-like calls are correct for 84 to 100% of the sources and FSRQ-like calls for 58 to 83%, depending on the sample. These samples come from spectroscopic follow-up and do not represent all BCUs. The candidates are fainter and lie closer to the Galactic plane than the labelled sources, and the excess of unclassified BCUs in the plane is not explained. We release the confidences of all 1623 BCUs.

titles.title: Classification of Fermi Blazars of Uncertain Type Using Positive-Unlabelled Machine Learning

abstracts.value: We study tensor perturbations and quasinormal modes (QNMs) of thick branes in $f(R,T)=R+αT$ gravity. Starting from the background thick brane solutions, we derive the Schrödinger-like equation for gravitational perturbations and construct the corresponding effective potential. The effective potential exhibits a double-barrier structure whose properties depend on the model parameters. We analyze transmission spectra and find good agreement between resonance peaks and the real parts of the quasinormal frequencies. The parameters $b$ and $α$ mainly control the width and height of the potential barriers, respectively. QNMs are extracted using both time-domain evolution and direct integration methods, showing consistent results for low-lying modes. Higher overtones become increasingly difficult to extract due to stronger damping and numerical contamination. Our results indicate that $f(R,T)$ corrections significantly affect both the effective potential and the quasinormal spectrum, providing a possible imprint of modified gravity in braneworld perturbations.

titles.title: Quasinormal modes of thick branes in $f(R,T)$ gravity

abstracts.value: The latest developments regarding the feasibility of muon-hadron collisions, achieved through the major reuse of LH$e$C infrastructure, are presented - at the LH$μ$C, a 1 or 2 TeV $μ^+$ beam collides with a 7 TeV proton beam, resulting in the $μ^+p$ centre-of-mass energy of 5.3 or 7.5 TeV, respectively, at an average luminosity close to $10^{34}$cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$. First, a concise scientific motivation is given, including exceptional prospects for neutrino science, and is followed by a presentation of the LH$μ$C concept in a nutshell - from the source of ultra-cold anti-muons, through the muon booster, to the main muon ring. Basic considerations regarding the machine-detector interface and the general-purpose detector are also presented. The paper concludes with an outlook underlying unique and powerful synergies between the LH$μ$C, LH$e$C, FCC and Muon Collider projects.

abstracts.value: In this work, we construct an asymptotically conical regular black hole in four-dimensional nonpolynomial quasitopological gravity. Starting from a linear choice of the reduced function, which yields an asymptotically conical Schwarzschild-like solution, we introduce a nonlinear deformation that preserves the leading asymptotic cone while producing an exact black hole solution with a de Sitter core and finite curvature invariants. We further establish the corresponding black hole thermodynamics for both solutions within the Hamiltonian and Wald frameworks. The entropy contains rational and logarithmic terms in the regular model, and both solutions satisfy the first law of black hole thermodynamics.

titles.title: An asymptotically conical regular black hole in four-dimensional nonpolynomial quasitopological gravity

abstracts.value: We identify the phase of a Bargmann invariant of two matter-wave interferometers as a quantum gravity signature that cannot be reproduced by any branchwise-definite classical gravitational field. For matter coupled linearly to linearized gravity, the interferometric coherence factorizes exactly into a conservative Newtonian phase, the characteristic functional of the graviton state, and a commutator phase. For Wigner-positive graviton states, the first two are classically reproducible; therefore, decoherence alone cannot certify that gravity is quantized. The Bargmann phase isolates the commutator, which is independent of the graviton state and of all Newtonian interactions and is bounded by which-path decoherence. For gravity, this radiation-reaction effect is sixty orders of magnitude below experimental reach, but trapped-ion analogs can test it at order unity.

titles.title: Bargmann-invariant witness of the graviton commutator

abstracts.value: Under explicit and physically motivated assumptions, we identify a local-to-global thermodynamic mechanism that organizes several previously disconnected inequalities on black holes. We first focus on asymptotically flat, static, and spherically-symmetric black holes, and provide a unified thermodynamic perspective on various Penrose-like inequalities. We also discuss the generalizations in asymptotically Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black holes/branes. In holographic settings, these bounds imply monotonic behavior of normalized thermodynamic quantities in the dual field theory. Notably, one central integrated inequality can be established directly under the NEC in general static planar symmetric asymptotically Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black branes. Our purpose is not to claim a fully general proof of the proposed local bounds, but to expose a unified structural perspective connecting local thermodynamic constraints to global geometric inequalities. Establishing the local bounds beyond the classes considered here remains an open problem.

titles.title: From Specific Heat Bounds to Penrose-like Inequalities: A Unified Thermodynamic Perspective

abstracts.value: We establish the existence of a new electromagnetic memory effect in all odd spacetime dimensions. This effect is a universal property of electromagnetic fields sourced by charged particles of constant momenta, appears at the Coulombic order and is directly related to the Weinberg soft theorem. We provide a unified derivation of this effect in all higher dimensions by evaluating the Maxwell constraint on a null plane at large, finite distance. We observe that in odd spacetime dimensions, the lightray integral computing the memory effect does not commute with the large-$r$ expansion. Our results necessarily assume that the lightray integral is taken prior to the $r \rightarrow \infty$ limit. The effect vanishes in the opposite order of limits, in agreement with previous results. We compute the Coulombic order electromagnetic memory effect for both massless and massive sources in all higher dimensions, explain its relation to the Fourier transform of the leading soft photon theorem and present a protocol for its measurement in a finite time parametrically larger than the distance of a detector from the sources. We conclude with comments on the generalization to gravity.

titles.title: On memory effects in odd spacetime dimensions

abstracts.value: We propose to study the Collins effect in the production of almost back-to-back unpolarized hadrons (mainly charged pions) by looking at their azimuthal distributions around the jet thrust-axis in the process $γγ\to h_1h_2X$. The quasi-real photons in the initial state can be emitted either by two scattering leptons or two charged heavy nuclei in ultra-peripheral collisions. We provide numerical estimates for kinematic configurations in principle accessible at the Future Circular Collider and at the planned experiments on ultra-peripheral collisions at the LHC. We find that the corresponding asymmetries can be sizable, even up to around 10-15%. The proposed measurements would thus shed light on the fragmentation mechanism of quarks into hadrons and, in principle, would allow one to distinguish among different existing models for the Collins functions.

titles.title: Probing the Collins effect at photon-photon colliders

abstracts.value: We investigate the three-dimensional (3D) stellar mass profiles of galaxy clusters using simulations and observations. We develop the Projection-to-Enclosed Estimator by Layers (PEEL) model, which geometrically reconstructs the 3D stellar mass profile from the projected stellar mass profile under the assumption of spherical symmetry. Starting from the outermost annulus, the PEEL model subtracts the contributions of the outer shells from the projected mass in each inner annulus. Using 205 halos from the TNG-Cluster simulation, we show that the reconstructed profile (hereafter the PEEL profile) recovers the true 3D stellar mass profile without systematic bias. We also examine potential systematic effects, including the use of subhalos versus stellar particles, the choice of cluster center, and the 3D shape of the halo. We then apply the PEEL model to a stacked sample of nine massive clusters from the MAssive Cluster survey with Hectospec (MACH). The observed PEEL profile is much flatter than the simulated 3D profile, indicating that the simulated clusters have a more centrally concentrated stellar mass distribution, mainly because of an excess of extremely massive galaxies in their cores. Combining the PEEL profile with the total mass profile from the caustic technique, we derive the stellar mass fraction profile of the observed clusters. The stellar mass fraction remains nearly constant at $0.009 \pm 0.002$ within $R_{200}$, consistent with previous observations and with the simulated clusters. The PEEL model provides a practical tool for measuring the 3D stellar mass profiles of large cluster samples from future wide-field spectroscopic surveys.

titles.title: Reconstructing the Three-Dimensional Stellar Mass Profiles of Massive Galaxy Clusters

abstracts.value: Nonlinear tides couple stellar oscillations and reshape the gravitational wave (GW) signal from inspiralling binaries. We present hydrodynamic simulations of nonlinear tides in inspiralling neutron-star binaries and, within a mode-coupling model, derive a semi-analytic quadrupolar fundamental mode-frequency shift through second order in the tidal strength. The two approaches agree in the perturbative regime, but diverge at stronger tidal fields, where perturbation theory breaks down. In the late inspiral, nonlinear tides reduce the fundamental-mode frequency by ${\sim}10\%$ for equal-mass binaries and add a GW phase shift of $\mathcal{O}(1)$ radian beyond the linear tidal response. These effects make nonlinear tides a promising target for next-generation GW detectors.

titles.title: Nonlinear Tides of Binary Neutron Stars

abstracts.value: X-ray images of supernova remnants provide important information regarding the spatial distribution of the physical and chemical parameters of the shocked plasma. Our objective is to provide a comprehensive and quantitative assessment of the similarities observed across narrow-band images and equivalent-width maps of a given supernova remnant. We also aim to perform comparative analyses between distinct remnants. We adopted two dendrogram-based techniques, namely a multivariate analysis and a deep-learning, graph-based approach (by exploring different metrics) for the study of Chandra X-ray maps of Cassiopeia A, G292.0+1.8, Tycho's SNR, Kepler's SNR, and W49B. We also tested the reliability of our results on synthetic X-ray maps produced from a 3D hydrodynamic simulation of Cassiopeia A. We identify clusters of narrow-band images (and equivalent-width maps) corresponding to emission lines of chemical elements that are expected to be synthesized in the same layers of the exploding star and/or that originate from plasma at similar temperatures. By comparing different objects, we clearly observe strong similarities among Type Ia remnants (namely Tycho's SNR and Kepler's SNR) and core-collapse remnants (Cassiopeia A and G292.0+1.8), with W49B being more similar to the latter objects. The methodology developed in this work provides a robust tool to measure the analogies and differences between narrow-band images and equivalent-width maps of a supernova remnant, offering clues on the distribution of the different chemical species and on the plasma temperature. Although tested on a limited sample of objects, the adoption of this tool for the classification of supernova remnants (Type Ia vs. core-collapse) yields promising results.

titles.title: Investigating supernova-remnant X-ray maps with dendrogram-based techniques

abstracts.value: From their discovery as radio pulsars to landmark multi-messenger observations of their mergers, double neutron stars have transformed our understanding of the extreme Universe and the formation of heavy elements (Drout et al. 2017; Abbott et al. 2017). Yet, uncertainties in their formation result in predicted merger rates spanning orders of magnitude (Tauris et al. 2017; Mandel & Broekgaarden 2022). The most critical stage occurs when a star is stripped of its hydrogen-rich envelope, causing the binary orbit to shrink drastically. Despite its fundamental role, the resulting tight binaries comprising a stripped star and neutron star have remained elusive. Here we report a $\sim$$3.4\,M_{\odot}$ stripped star (Ludwig et al. 2026; Drout et al. 2023; Götberg et al. 2023) orbiting an unseen companion every 4.2 hours. Our orbital and spectroscopic analysis excludes a normal star, which would not fit within the orbit, as well as a second stripped star which would have been detectable in our spectra. Adding constraints from high cadence photometry gives a 99.4% probability that the companion is too massive to be a white dwarf, making a neutron star the most likely companion. We model the system's future and predict that the stripped star will transfer mass again before exploding as a hydrogen-free supernova, leaving a bound pair of neutron stars that will merge after 220 Myr. This system reveals a previously unconstrained phase of binary evolution, uncovering a new class of systems that probes the uncertain physics of massive stars, linking to observable gravitational-wave sources.

titles.title: An Intermediate Mass Stripped Star in a 4.2-hour Orbit around a Compact Object

abstracts.value: Kaonic atoms provide a unique experimental tool to investigate low-energy strong interactions in systems containing strangeness and, through high-lying transitions, to test bound-state quantum electrodynamics. The SIDDHARTA-2 experiment at the DA$Φ$NE electron--positron collider performs high-precision X-ray spectroscopy of kaonic atoms using low-momentum charged kaons produced in $ϕ$-meson decays. Its primary goal is the study of kaonic deuterium through the measurement of X-ray transitions to the ground state, providing direct access to the low-energy $K^-d$ interaction. In parallel, SIDDHARTA-2 has carried out a broad experimental programme with gaseous targets, including kaonic helium-4 and kaonic neon, as well as measurements of high-$n$ transitions in intermediate-mass kaonic atoms formed in the materials of the experimental setup. In this paper, the main SIDDHARTA-2 measurements and their physics motivations are reviewed, together with the experimental strategy developed for kaonic deuterium and the future perspectives of the collaboration within the EXKALIBUR programme.

titles.title: Kaonic Atom Measurements with the SIDDHARTA-2 Experiment at the DA$Φ$NE accelerator

abstracts.value: Universal fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computers are expected to require millions of physical qubits; yet extending the prevailing dedicated-control-line paradigm to this scale would exceed the wiring density and cooling-power budget of dilution refrigerators. Microwave frequency-division multiplexing (FDM) revolutionized classical communications by enabling many independent channels to share common transmission infrastructure. Translating this principle to superconducting quantum control, however, requires an all-microwave architecture and experimental validation of frequency-multiplexed gate control. Recent work in quantum error correction has demonstrated microwave-based readout, single-qubit gates and leakage suppression, whereas two-qubit gates remain predominantly driven by unipolar pulses and thus constitute the missing element of an all-microwave architecture. Here, we propose a periodically extensible hybrid multiplexing framework in which all gate operations are frequency-division multiplexed using polychromatic microwave pulses and band-pass filters, thereby reducing the required control-line count by one to two orders of magnitude. In a 1:4 demonstration, we achieve average errors of $(6.4\pm0.2)\times10^{-3}$ for parallel FDM CZ gates and $(10.6\pm0.2)\times10^{-4}$ for parallel FDM $XY(π/2)$ gates, without statistically significant multiplexing-induced degradation. Together with on-chip DC sources, this FDM-based gate-control scheme completes the last missing module in a scalable multiplexed-control architecture toward universal fault-tolerant quantum computing.

titles.title: A Control Line Multiplexing Framework for Scalable Quantum Computing

abstracts.value: The integration of bidirectional (V2G) charging allows electric vehicle (EV) fleets to operate as distributed energy assets. However, the joint optimization of charging schedules and trip assignments is NP-hard. Moreover, bidirectional power flows create non-monotonic state-of-charge (SoC) dynamics that weaken standard dual-based Benders cuts. We propose a hybrid quantum-classical Benders decomposition framework. To overcome the qubit overhead associated with encoding feasibility cuts, we introduce logic-based conflict cuts, which require near-zero auxiliary qubits. Furthermore, we develop a sparse recursive SoC formulation that reduces the constraint-matrix density by a factor of T/3 in the horizon length T. We demonstrate that our framework recovers MILP-optimal solutions on benchmark instances with a low auxiliary-qubit budget, and, as a minimal proof of concept, we execute a small instance end-to-end on IBM quantum hardware.

titles.title: Quantum-Classical Framework for the Joint Optimization of Bidirectional EV Charging and Trip Assignment

abstracts.value: A new barrel-type silicon detector has been constructed in the central rapidity region of the sPHENIX experiment as part of its charged-particle tracking system. The detector, referred to as the intermediate silicon tracker (INTT), provides single-event timing capability and contributes to charged-particle tracking in combination with the silicon-pixel vertex detector and the time-projection chamber. The INTT consists of two cylindrical barrels with full azimuthal coverage. The inner and outer barrels comprise 24 and 32 silicon strip ladders, respectively. Each ladder consists of four silicon strip sensors, covering the pseudorapidity range $|η| < 1.07$ for collision vertices within $\pm~10$ cm along the beam axis, at radial distances between 72 and 103 mm. The INTT has been fully integrated into the sPHENIX data acquisition system, with detector signals processed by eight FELIX servers. Continuous data taking is enabled by a streaming readout mode, in which detector data are accumulated without hardware triggers, while a conventional trigger-based mode is also supported. The detector achieves stable operation, small inactive area, and high efficiency, providing precise timing, tracking, and vertexing performance during the collection of beam-beam collision data.

titles.title: The Intermediate Silicon Tracker Detector for sPHENIX

abstracts.value: We propose a hybrid quantum-classical method for reconstructing energy-level degeneracies and thermodynamic properties of spin systems. A single ancilla qubit is used to measure the partition function at imaginary inverse temperatures. For spectra lying on a known equally spaced energy grid, the inverse discrete Fourier transform allows exact reconstruction of degeneracies in the absence of noise, without spectral leakage. The quantum circuits are optimized using commuting interactions and Eulerian ordering. We demonstrate the method for frustrated Ising antiferromagnets on periodic Kagome graphs with up to 36 spins, using the ibm_kingston quantum processor. Despite substantial circuit depth and hardware noise, the reconstructed spectra retain their dominant features, and the calculated heat capacities reproduce the main temperature dependence of the exact results. Keywords: partition function, imaginary temperature, Ising model, heat capacity, ancilla qubit, quantum computing.

titles.title: Quantum computation of energy level degeneracy and thermodynamical properties of spin systems

abstracts.value: Rydberg-atom sensors have emerged as a promising quantum technology for broadband radio-frequency detection owing to their intrinsic calibration, wide frequency coverage, and high sensitivity. However, their potential for intelligent identification of real-world wireless signals remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate a quantum-enabled framework for mobile signal classification based on Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency spectroscopy and deep learning. Three types of wireless emissions, including cellular voice call, Wi-Fi, and 5G signals from three commercial smartphone brands, are measured to construct a spectral-fingerprint dataset. A convolutional neural network trained on this dataset achieves an initial baseline classification accuracy of 93.44%. To compensate for spectral drifts induced by temporal and environmental variations, a progressive fine-tuning strategy is employed to continuously adapt the pretrained model, enabling robust classification across diverse deployment scenarios. Furthermore, continuous real-time monitoring is demonstrated under dynamically varying wireless conditions, including cellular voice call, Wi-Fi, and their coexistence. The proposed system achieves an overall frame-level recognition accuracy of 87.67% over a 60-s measurement. These results establish a pathway toward intelligent quantum radio-frequency sensing and highlight the potential of Rydberg-atom platforms for real-time wireless signal awareness and spectrum monitoring.

titles.title: Spectral fingerprint recognition of mobile signals via Rydberg atomic sensors

abstracts.value: In quantum simulation of electronic structure it is often expected that the estimate of the ground energy converges to the continuum basis limit at a rate of $\mathcal O(N^{-1})$ for a basis of size $N$. This has been found in analytical and numerical studies, but without a rigorous treatment of the error in the quantities considered in quantum algorithms. Here we show the $\mathcal O(N^{-1})$ scaling of the error for a wide range of cases needed for quantum simulation of chemistry. We show the error in the ground energy scales as $\mathcal O(N^{-1})$ for plane-wave as well as spatial grid bases. For the spatial grid we consider both a periodic system and a non-periodic system with open boundaries. For time evolution, our bound on the error in the state itself is weaker than $\mathcal O(N^{-1})$, but we show that the error in observables scales as $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(N^{-1})$ in important cases. In particular, we may consider a smoothed observable that describes the position of particles. We show that this error scales as $\mathcal O(N^{-5/3}+tN^{-1})$ for time $t$, again both for plane-wave and spatial grid bases. For the non-periodic grid case we use a condition that the true evolution would not result in significant leakage past the boundaries, which introduces basis error unrelated to the resolution of the discretisation. We also show the error in the kinetic energy of a particle scales as $\mathcal O((t+\log N)/N)$ for the plane-wave and grid bases. Together, these results show that $\mathcal O(N^{-1})$ scaling of the error holds for many of the relevant cases for quantum algorithms (with a trivial log factor for kinetic energy).

titles.title: Basis-set error bounds for first-quantised quantum simulation of chemistry

abstracts.value: We study periodic orbits of charged particles in the equatorial plane of a five-dimensional ($D=5$) rotating Myers--Perry black hole (BH) immersed in a uniform magnetic field, and the gravitational waves emitted by these orbits in an extreme mass-ratio inspiral. All results are compared with the Kerr BH in the uniform magnetic field. We find that a charged particle is much more weakly bound to the $D=5$ dimensional BH, i.e. its energy at the innermost stable circular orbit is close to unity, $0.95$--$0.99$, compared with $0.78$--$0.94$ for the Kerr BH, and the depth of the potential well is several times smaller. As a result, the periodic orbits of the $D=5$ dimensional BH lie much closer to the separatrix. The magnetic field can make the azimuthal frequency of the orbit smaller than the radial one and produces loops in the orbits far from the BH. Using the numerical kludge method, we compute the gravitational waveforms for a compact object of $10M_\odot$ orbiting a BH of $10^6M_\odot$. At the same magnetic field, the $D=5$ dimensional signal has a longer period, lower frequencies, and an amplitude smaller by about $18\%$. We show that for the magnetic parameter $βM=0.02$ the strongest spectral line is at $7.9$ mHz, compared with $9.9$ mHz for the Kerr BH. An estimate of the radiation reaction shows that the periodic orbits survive from less than an hour to a few days in the presence of an external magnetic field. Over these lifetimes, the signal-to-noise ratio for LISA is $7$--$31$ for the rotating BH in $D=5$ dimensions, compared to the Kerr BH where it is about $15$--$54$.

titles.title: Gravitational-Wave Signatures and Periodic Orbits of Charged Particles Around a Five-Dimensional Rotating Black Hole: Comparison with the Kerr Black Hole

abstracts.value: We revisit the supernova constraints on three well-motivated light gauge bosons: the dark photon, the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson, and the $U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ gauge boson. For the dark photon and the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson, we re-evaluate the nucleon bremsstrahlung process within the one-pion exchange approximation, retaining the full momentum and mass dependence. The geometrical dependence of the decay and absorption of these gauge bosons inside the supernova core is also taken into account. Updated bounds on these models are derived based on the cooling of SN1987A and energy deposition constraints from low-energy supernovae (LESNe). Taking the SFHo-18.8 $18.8\,M_\odot$ profile, the SN1987A cooling constraints reach masses of about $230$ MeV, $280$ MeV, and $300$ MeV for the dark photon, the $U(1)_{B-L}$ boson, and the $U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ boson, while the corresponding LESN limits extend to about $450$ MeV, $440$ MeV, and $600$ MeV, respectively. The kinetic mixing parameter $ε$ for dark photon, the gauge coupling $g_{BL}$ in the $U(1)_{B-L}$ model, and the gauge coupling $g_{μτ}$ for the $U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ model are constrained down to $5.8\times10^{-12}$, $2.9\times10^{-16}$, and $6.4\times10^{-12}$, respectively.

titles.title: Revisiting supernova constraints on dark gauge bosons

abstracts.value: We characterize quasiclassical state conversion under thermal operations through population capacities: the maximum population that thermal operations can concentrate on each set of energy levels. These capacities form a normalized, nondecreasing submodular rank function whose base polytope is exactly the thermally reachable population region. Their bounds therefore provide a complete system of accessibility constraints. Every nested chain of capacities can be simultaneously saturated by a reachable state, yielding the maximum expectation value of any prescribed observable, including the system Hamiltonian. For a prescribed target, its thermomajorization prefixes suffice to certify exact conversion through at most $n-1$ binary work-extraction probes. For approximate conversion, we construct a distinguished reachable state from active capacity constraints using a weighted principal sequence in $O(n^2 \log n)$ operations. At fixed comparison weights, this state minimizes every weighted convex separable residual cost and realizes a common first contact with the corresponding target-centered smoothing regions. Finally, the optimal trace-distance error equals the largest capacity advantage of the target over the initial state. This gap is attained at a target prefix and equals the largest positive optimized energy-storage deficit among the same binary probes, divided by their energy gap. Thus a common population capacity geometry determines accessibility, observable optimization, conversion certificates, and universal approximation.

titles.title: Population Capacity and the Geometry of Thermomajorization

abstracts.value: The recently discovered IR phase of QCD is characterized by an infrared (IR) sector of Dirac modes that separates and dynamically decouples from the bulk of the spectrum, becoming scale invariant in the process [1]. Among key features of this IR sector is the negative power-law behavior of Dirac spectral density near zero with power $p$ close to $-1$. Here we start investigating to what extent can this behavior be mimicked by chiral Anderson models. In particular, we study 3-D chiral-orthogonal systems with logarithmic off-diagonal disorder where negative-power ``spikes'' have been observed [2]. We find that at finite disorder strength $W$ of moderate strength, these models in fact do not have a power-singular density of states (DOS) at zero energy in the thermodynamic limit. Rather, this power $p_1$ vanishes and the spectrum features a very accurate power behavior with $p<0$ on an interval around $E = 1$ spreading increasingly closer to $E=0$ and $E = \infty$ with increasing $W$. We connect this to the fact that random hoppings $t$ in these quantum systems are drawn from a scale-invariant $1/t$ distribution regularized via $t \in [e^{-W/2}, e^{W/2}]$, and DOS with negative power can naturally arise inside that range. We show that $\lim_{W \to \infty} p(W, E)=-1$ for all energies accessible by our data. This indicates that, upon removing the cutoff $W$, quantum mechanics transforms the scale-invariant $1/t$ noise into a scale-invariant $1/E$ distribution of eigenstates, which mimics the interpretation of scale-invariant Dirac spectral densities in the IR phase as being due to scale-invariant glue backgrounds [1]. Our results imply that, to model the IR sector of the IR phase, the IR cutoff in chiral Anderson systems needs to be viewed as descending from the randomness strength $W$ rather than the lattice size $L$.

titles.title: Negative-Power Density of States in Chiral-Orthogonal Disordered Systems and the IR Phase of QCD
